newsitem.title: USA: Calif. legislature paves way for state tobacco suit.
newsitem.headline: Calif. legislature paves way for state tobacco suit.

text.p: California's legislature gave final approval on Wednesday to a bill clearing the way for the state to sue major tobacco companies to recoup public health-care costs related to smoking.
The state Assembly approved the bill on a vote of 64-10, sending it to Republican Gov. Pete Wilson.
Wilson's spokesman, Sean Walsh, said the governor intended to sign the bill and to call on the state attorney general to immediately file a lawsuit against the tobacco industry.
The bill was passed by the state Senate this week.

The measure, by Assembly Speaker Cruz Bustamante, removes any legal barriers to California's attorney general filing suit against tobacco companies to recover state-paid medical costs of treating smokers.
Opponents of the bill, mostly Republican lawmakers, had argued that the state collects more in taxes from smokers than it spends to treat them for smoking-related illnesses.

California, the most populous state with billions of dollars in potential claims, has so far not sued major tobacco companies. But pressure has been building on state lawmakers in recent months to join the legal battle.

Republican state Attorney General Dan Lungren has long maintained that a state lawsuit against tobacco companies would fail because of a 1987 California law shielding them from product liability claims.

Bustamante said his bill would amend that law, allowing Lungren to join other states in suing the tobacco industry. Once signed into law by Wilson, Bustamante's urgency legislation would take effect immediately.
